summary.oneLiner: Century Extrusions Limited is an aluminium extrusion manufacturer operating an integrated facility at Kharagpur, supplying OEMs and industrial customers across infrastructure, electrical, transportation, defence and engineering applications.
summary.business: The Company manufactures aluminium extrusion products, producing 13,325 MT during FY 2025-26 against 13,433 MT in the previous year. It serves OEMs and industrial customers across sectors such as infrastructure, electrical, transportation, defence, engineering, packaging, irrigation and marine, positioning itself as an engineering partner that translates customer requirements into reliable solutions rather than a commodity profile supplier.

currentContext.strategies: Improve operational efficiency, increase the share of value-added products and deepen engagement with high-value applications|Make the Kharagpur brownfield expansion central to the forward agenda - not only adding tonnage but enhancing readiness for the next phase of demand and enabling faster response and more specialised applications|Strengthen the capital base and financial flexibility through a proposed Rights Issue of up to Rs. 45 crore to support long-term growth plans|Modernise the manufacturing ecosystem through technology - implementation of SAP HANA during the year, plus better monitoring, improved inspection systems and stronger process controls|Sustain globally accepted quality certifications as a differentiator that enables the Company to serve demanding customer applications|Build market presence in key end-use sectors, deepening engagement with customers in automotive, power, defence and aerospace-related segments, supported by participation in industry forums and exhibitions including Alumex and Automechanika|Operate a customer-centric model aimed at becoming a dependable partner in the customer's manufacturing or project journey rather than a seller of profiles
currentContext.expansion: The Company operates an integrated manufacturing facility at Kharagpur with an installed extrusion capacity of 15,000 MTPA, described as providing the flexibility and precision to serve diverse customer needs. A brownfield expansion at the same Kharagpur site is ongoing and is expected to add 9,000 MT of capacity; management describes it as central to the Company's future agenda, aimed not only at adding tonnage but at strengthening manufacturing flexibility, service capability and readiness to serve more specialised applications in the next phase of demand. No commissioning date, ramp schedule or rupee project cost is stated in the routed text. Funding-side, the Board approved raising up to Rs. 45 Crores by way of a Rights Issue (Draft Letter of Offer filed with the Stock Exchange on 24th April 2026, in-principle approval pending), and the Company retained the entire FY 2025-26 profits in the business, recommending no dividend, in view of its capital requirement and growth.

risks.risk: Input-cost volatility: aluminium prices, energy costs and freight expenses
risks.note: The Board's Risk Management and Mitigation section lists industry and market risk first, noting that volatility in aluminium prices, energy costs and freight expenses can affect input cost structures and margins in a competitive environment. As a converter buying aluminium and selling extrusions, the company's margin is a spread; it relies on cost optimisation, sourcing strategies, product-mix improvement and value-added applications rather than on any disclosed hedging or pass-through mechanism.

risks.risk: Demand is tied to the infrastructure, construction, transportation and industrial capex cycle
risks.note: The AR states demand for extrusions is closely linked to infrastructure, construction, transportation and industrial activity, and that macroeconomic slowdowns or delays in projects can impact volumes. Mitigation is customer and sector diversification plus close monitoring of project pipelines and capital expenditure trends - i.e. the order book follows third-party capex decisions the company does not control.

risks.risk: Competition from unorganised players and low-cost imports under changing trade policy
risks.note: Management flags competition from both organised and unorganised players, coupled with low-cost imports and changing trade policies, as able to pressure pricing and market share. This is a structural pricing-power constraint: the stated defence is quality, reliability, customised OEM solutions and service levels, not scale or a cost advantage.

risks.risk: Technology and capability obsolescence requiring continuous reinvestment
risks.note: The risk chapter cites rapid technological change and rising customer expectations requiring continuous upgrades in process efficiency, automation and engineering capabilities, mitigated by investments in advanced manufacturing, digital systems, quality assurance and die development. This makes maintenance/upgrade capex a recurring claim on cash flow to defend the value-added product mix.

risks.risk: Rising environmental and safety regulation may force additional operating and capital spend
risks.note: The AR states that increasing environmental and safety regulations may necessitate additional operational and capital investments, mitigated by a compliance-driven culture and progressive adoption of sustainability, safety and environment-friendly practices. For an energy-intensive extrusion plant this is an open-ended, non-discretionary cost line.

risks.risk: Funding dependence: earnings fully retained, no dividend, and a Rs 45 crore rights issue still awaiting exchange approval
risks.note: The Board recommended no dividend, stating that in view of meeting the capital requirement and for growth the entire profits are being re-invested back into the company. Separately, the Board approved raising up to Rs 45 crore by a rights issue on 11th February 2026 and filed the Draft Letter of Offer on 24th April 2026, with the company still in the process of obtaining in-principle approval from the stock exchanges as at the date of the report. Growth funding therefore depends on an equity raise that was not complete at reporting date, and carries dilution for non-participating holders.

risks.risk: Promoter-family leadership succession and independent-director churn
risks.note: Mr Vikram Jhunjhunwala, re-appointed Chairman & Managing Director for three years from 12th February 2025 and confirmed by postal ballot with 99.70% in favour, resigned w.e.f. 2nd June 2025 under the Board's succession plan, and his son Mr Shivanshu Jhunjhunwala was appointed CMD from 3rd June 2025 to 2nd June 2028. In the same window independent director Mrs Suhita Mukhopadhyay retired on expiry of her second term (7th September 2025) and Mr Sanjeev Kishore resigned w.e.f. 7th April 2026, with Mr Charan Singh appointed thereafter. Executive authority sits with a single promoter family and the independent bench turned over twice within roughly a year.

risks.risk: Single-product concentration with flat physical volumes
risks.note: The only manufacturing disclosure is aluminium extrusions, and production was 13325 MT in FY2025-26 against 13,433 MT in FY2024-25 - a marginal decline. The company describes itself as operating in a dynamic aluminium extrusion industry with no second product line or segment disclosed, so growth in the period came from realisation and mix rather than from throughput, and there is no diversified activity to offset an extrusion-cycle downturn.
